A.explanation: With $X_1$ to $Y_1$ the supply connects to the $Y_1$-$Y_2$ wire, but with $X_2$ to $Y_2$ that wire ends at the open $Y_2$ contact and no complete loop to the lamp is formed.

B.explanation: With $X_1$ to $Y_1$ the supply reaches the $Y_1$-$Y_2$ wire, but with $X_2$ to $Z_2$ the lamp side connects to the $Z_2$ wire which is not joined to the supply in diagram 2.

C.explanation: With $X_1$ to $Z_1$ the supply is correctly fed toward $X_1$, but with $X_2$ to $Y_2$ the lamp side connects to the $Y_1$-$Y_2$ wire which is left floating.

D.explanation: With $X_1$ to $Z_1$ and $X_2$ to $Z_2$ the supply current can travel via $Z_1$ to $X_1$ then to $Z_2$ then to $X_2$ and the lamp, completing the circuit back to the supply.

hints: Trace diagram 2 from the top supply terminal: note that $Z_1$ is now wired to the supply and $X_1$ is wired to $Z_2$.
Remember the lamp lights only if there is an unbroken conducting path from the supply, through both changeover switches, through the lamp, and back to the supply.
Test each $X_1$ position to see which wire it energises, then check which $X_2$ position joins that same energised wire to the lamp.
walkthrough: Identify the rewired paths in diagram 2: the lower supply wire goes to $Z_1$, the upper supply wire goes to $X_1$ via the left loop, and $X_1$ is also linked by the top loop to $Z_2$.
State the rule for lighting: current needs a continuous loop supply to lamp to supply, so both switch blades $X_1$ and $X_2$ must select contacts that belong to the same continuous conductor.
Consider $X_1$ to $Z_1$: the blade joins the lower supply wire at $Z_1$ to the $X_1$ conductor, which is connected to $Z_2$, so the $Z_2$ terminal becomes live.
Consider $X_1$ to $Y_1$ instead: the blade would join the $X_1$ conductor to the $Y_1$-$Y_2$ wire, leaving the $Z_2$ wire disconnected from the supply.
Now look at the right-hand switch: the lamp is wired to the blade $X_2$, so the lamp is lit only if $X_2$ touches the live incoming wire, which from step 3 is $Z_2$.
Therefore the combination $X_1$ to $Z_1$ together with $X_2$ to $Z_2$ gives supply to $Z_1$ to $X_1$ to $Z_2$ to $X_2$ to lamp to supply. This is option D.
